description: Evolved Energy Research publishes a detailed Excel workbook of model results for the U.S. carbon-neutral pathways study by Williams and colleagues. The file sits beside a separate RIO input-summary workbook in the study's GitHub repository. The article describes eight decarbonisation scenarios plus a reference case covering U.S. energy and industrial carbon dioxide through 2050. EnergyPATHWAYS models end-use demand for 16 U.S. regions; RIO models energy-supply investment and sampled hourly operations. The workbook is a published scenario output, not measured infrastructure performance. Its geographic scope is the United States, with regional and temporal detail determined by the underlying model tables. GitHub provides the file as an XLSX download under repository MIT terms at no charge. The article says the repository holds extended model results and cost-related input data, but the workbook's individual sheets were not opened in this metadata review. That is a limit on field-level interpretation. These outputs can be used to compare electricity, fuel and transport transition assumptions in new capacity-planning simulations. The related U.S. case application is documented by the cited paper; the current EnergyPATHWAYS code is a separate G7 draft.
